html:
An ancient Egyptian obelisk that Theodosius I set up in the Hippodrome of Constantinople in 390. It was first raised about 1450 BCE by the pharaoh Thutmose III at the temple of Karnak in Egypt.

The obelisk was shipped down the Nile to Alexandria in the 4th century and waited there for decades before Theodosius had it brought to his capital. Only the upper part survives; the rest probably broke in transport. It stands about 20 m high with its base, and its pink granite and hieroglyphs still look sharp.

The marble base is a work of its own time. Its reliefs show Theodosius and his family in the imperial box, watching races, receiving gifts from defeated enemies and holding out a victory wreath. One side shows the obelisk being raised. It still stands where it was put, in today's Sultanahmet Square.
sum: An ancient Egyptian obelisk that Theodosius I set up in the Hippodrome of Constantinople in 390. It was first raised about 1450 BCE by the pharaoh Thutmose III at the temple of Karnak in Egypt.
